literal: Love having forsaken, oneself having afflicted, virtue without considering, accumulated splendid wealth will be taken by others.
translation: Others will possess the splendid wealth accumulated by one who has forsaken love, afflicted oneself with deprivation, and disregarded virtue.
modern: அன்பைத் துறந்து, தன்னைத் தானே வருத்திக்கொண்டு, அறத்தையும் போற்றாமல் சேர்த்த சிறந்த செல்வத்தை மற்றவர்கள் எடுத்துக் கொள்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of hoarding wealth through extreme greed. The poet explains that when a person accumulates 'splendid wealth' (ஒண்பொருள்) by abandoning love for fellow beings (அன்பொரீஇ), starving and afflicting their own body (தற்செற்று), and completely ignoring righteous deeds (அறநோக்காது), they do not get to enjoy it. Instead, that hard-earned wealth ultimately falls into the hands of strangers or others (பிறர் கொள்வார்). The verse teaches that wealth gathered without compassion, self-care, or virtue is entirely wasted on the hoarder.
